The Artemis II Orion capsule is a 16.5-foot-wide spacecraft with roughly 330 cubic feet of habitable living space, providing roughly the volume of two minivans for the four-person crew. The capsule stands 11 feet tall (excluding the service module) and is roughly 60% larger than the Apollo command modules. Key Size Features of the Orion Capsule: Habitable Space: 330 cubic feet (approx. 9.3 cubic meters). Diameter: 16.5 feet (roughly 5 meters). Height: 11 feet. Capacity: 4 crew members. Comparison and Context: Vs. Apollo: The Orion capsule has 330 cubic feet of space, compared to the 210 cubic feet in Apollo command modules. Components: The crew resides in the crew module, which features a 16.5-foot heat shield. Functionality: While small, the capsule includes a toilet, medical kit, and exercise equipment.
